title: Uniform bounded enlargement inside a weak presheaf monomorphism
statement:
Fix an input universe as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a small ordinary category and $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Set})$. Let $1$ be its terminal presheaf and $I$ a presheaf with maps $e_0,e_1:1\to I$ such that $\delta=(e_0,e_1):1\amalg1\to I$ is monic. For $i:U\to V$ and $j:K\to L$, put $i\square j:(V\times K)\amalg_{U\times K}(U\times L)\to V\times L$. Let $\mathrm{An}$ be the closure of a small set of monomorphisms under isomorphisms, pushouts, small transfinite compositions and arrow retracts. Assume $e_\varepsilon\square j\in\mathrm{An}$ for every monomorphism $j$ and $\varepsilon=0,1$, and $\delta\square i\in\mathrm{An}$ for every $i\in\mathrm{An}$. A map has the right lifting property against a class if every commutative square with left side in that class has a diagonal filler. Call a map naive fibrant if it has the right lifting property against $\mathrm{An}$, and an object $Z$ naive fibrant if $Z\to1$ is such a map. Write $[K,Z]_I$ for maps $K\to Z$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by the endpoint restrictions of maps $K\times I\to Z$. Let $W_I$ be the maps $u:K\to L$ for which $[L,Z]_I\to[K,Z]_I$ is bijective for every naive fibrant $Z$ in the input universe.

There is an infinite cardinal $\alpha$ in the input universe, greater than $|\operatorname{Mor}(A)|$, with the following uniform property. For every monomorphism $X\hookrightarrow Y$ in $W_I$ and every subpresheaf $U\subseteq Y$ of size less than $\alpha$, there is a subpresheaf $V\subseteq Y$ of size less than $\alpha$ containing $U$ such that $V\cap X\hookrightarrow V$ belongs to $W_I$. Here the size of a presheaf $F$ is the cardinality of $\coprod_{a\in\operatorname{Ob}(A)}F(a)$, intersections are computed objectwise, and the cardinal is independent of $X,Y,U$. No model structure is assumed.

source.place: Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, Lemma 2.4.38, with the cardinal chosen as in Lemma 2.4.37, printed pp. 65-66 (PDF pp. 80-81). Total-element size is equivalent to the category-of-elements size used there once the bound exceeds the size of A. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this interval-homotopy lemma.

proof.text: First, for every naive fibrant $Z$, direct $I$-homotopy of maps $K\to Z$ is already an equivalence relation. Constant homotopies give reflexivity. Given homotopies $h:u\sim v$ and $k:u\sim w$, put them on the two faces $I\times\{0,1\}\times K$ and put the constant $u$ on $\{0\}\times I\times K$. They agree on intersections. The union's inclusion in $I\times I\times K$ is $e_0\square(\delta\times K)$, hence is anodyne by the hypothesis. A filler into $Z$ restricts on $\{1\}\times I\times K$ to a homotopy $v\sim w$. Taking $w=u$ gives symmetry, and applying this operation to $v\sim u$ and $v\sim w$ gives transitivity. Thus equality in $[K,Z]_I$ is represented by one homotopy.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.24, three-face filling argument, written out.

proof.text: Every $a:K\to L$ in $\mathrm{An}$ belongs to $W_I$: a map $K\to Z$ extends by naive fibrancy, giving surjectivity. For injectivity, if $f_0,f_1:L\to Z$ have equal restricted classes, Step 1 gives a homotopy on $K$. This and $f_0,f_1$ glue on $(I\times K)\amalg_{\{0,1\}\times K}(\{0,1\}\times L)$. Its inclusion in $I\times L$ is $\delta\square a\in\mathrm{An}$, so a filler is a homotopy between $f_0,f_1$. Also $W_I$ has two-out-of-three: precomposition respects homotopies, and the composite testing function is the composite of the two testing functions; two bijections among these three imply the third is a bijection.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.25 and Remark 2.4.21, before the model structure.

proof.text: Choose a small set $\Lambda$ generating $\mathrm{An}$. Apply [lem-coef-presheaf-bounded-intersection-replacement] with $B=I$. Obtain $R,\eta,\lambda<\alpha$ and all its numbered properties. The objects $R(F)$ are naive fibrant: they lift against $\Lambda$, and lifting extends to its weak saturation. More explicitly, a right lifting class is closed under arrow retracts by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]; on the left, pushouts and finite compositions preserve lifting by that same statement, and continuous transfinite compositions preserve it by [lem-coef-transfinite-left-lifting]. Thus every generator lifting extends to every map of $\mathrm{An}$. By Step 2, every $\eta_F$ is in $W_I$. Fix a weak monomorphism $i:X\hookrightarrow Y$. Functoriality gives $R(i)\eta_X=\eta_Yi$, so two-out-of-three shows that the monomorphism $k=R(i):R(X)\hookrightarrow R(Y)$ lies in $W_I$.

source.place: Construction 2.4.36, Lemma 2.4.37 and the first paragraph of Lemma 2.4.38. The separate ranks correct the later size inference.

proof.text: The presheaf category is locally finitely presentable by [lem-coef-presheaf-local-finite-presentability]; its Hom sets are small subsets of products of component function sets. Apply [lem-coef-accessible-small-object-factorization] to $\Lambda$ and the arrow $k$, obtaining $k=qj$ with $j\in\mathrm{An}$ and $q\in\Lambda^\square$. The lifting-closure and transfinite-lifting statements used in Step 3 show $q\in\mathrm{An}^\square$. Since $j,k\in W_I$, two-out-of-three gives $q\in W_I$. Its codomain is the naive fibrant $R(Y)$, so [lem-coef-presheaf-naive-fibration-whitehead] says $q$ lifts against every monomorphism. Lift the square with top $j$, left $k$, right $q$, and bottom $1_{R(Y)}$. Its diagonal $d:R(Y)\to\operatorname{cod}(j)$ satisfies $dk=j$ and $qd=1$. Therefore the arrow maps $(1,d):k\to j$ and $(1,q):j\to k$ exhibit $k$ as a retract of $j$. The assumed retract closure of $\mathrm{An}$ proves $k\in\mathrm{An}$.

source.place: Corollary 2.4.29, with the small-object, Whitehead, and retract arguments supplied explicitly; used in Proposition 2.4.34 and Lemma 2.4.38.

proof.text: Since $R(X)$ is naive fibrant, the identity of $R(X)$ extends across $k\in\mathrm{An}$ to a map $r:R(Y)\to R(X)$ satisfying $rk=1$. On $(I\times R(X))\amalg_{\{0,1\}\times R(X)}(\{0,1\}\times R(Y))$ define a map to $R(Y)$ by $k\operatorname{pr}_{R(X)}$ on the cylinder over $R(X)$, and by $(1_{R(Y)},kr)$ on its two other faces. The formulas agree because $rk=1$. The inclusion of this union in $I\times R(Y)$ is $\delta\square k\in\mathrm{An}$, so naive fibrancy of $R(Y)$ supplies a map $h:I\times R(Y)\to R(Y)$ with $h_0=1$, $h_1=kr$, and $h|_{I\times R(X)}=k\operatorname{pr}_{R(X)}$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.33 and Proposition 2.4.34: the strong deformation retraction is constructed by two specified fillers, not assumed.

proof.text: For any $T\subseteq Y$ of size $<\alpha$, the image $E_T$ of $I\times R(T)$ under $h$ has size $<\alpha$ by property (3) of [lem-coef-presheaf-bounded-intersection-replacement]. For each total element $z$ of $E_T$, property (4) gives a subpresheaf $T_z\subseteq Y$ of size $<\alpha$ with $z\in R(T_z)$. The collection of subpresheaves of $Y$ is a small set (it is coded by subsets of the total-element set of $Y$); well-order it by [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem] and choose its least eligible $T_z$. Put $T^+=T\cup\bigcup_{z\in E_T}T_z$. There are fewer than $\alpha$ summands, so regularity makes $|T^+|<\alpha$. Functoriality and preservation of monomorphisms give $R(T_z)\subseteq R(T^+)$, whence $h(I\times R(T))\subseteq R(T^+)$. This defines a fixed enlargement rule on all small subpresheaves of $Y$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.38, middle paragraph: small support for the homotopy image, with the cardinality and witness choices explicit.

proof.text: Starting with the given $U$, use [lem-weil-pbc-transfinite-recursion] on the initial ordinal $\lambda$ to form $V_0=U$, $V_{\xi+1}=V_\xi^+$ by Step 6, and $V_\xi=\bigcup_{\zeta<\xi}V_\zeta$ at every nonzero limit $\xi<\lambda$. The recursion rule may return $U$ on an incoherent prefix; induction shows that this fallback never occurs. The invariant is that these are increasing subpresheaves containing $U$, each of size $<\alpha$, with $h(I\times R(V_\xi))\subseteq R(V_{\xi+1})$ at every successor. At limits, the number of earlier terms is $<\lambda<\alpha$, so regularity verifies the size invariant. Set $V=\bigcup_{\xi<\lambda}V_\xi$. Since $\lambda<\alpha$, regularity also gives $|V|<\alpha$ at this final union. Property (5) of [lem-coef-presheaf-bounded-intersection-replacement] gives $R(V)=\bigcup_{\xi<\lambda}R(V_\xi)$. Thus every element of $I\times R(V)$ lies in $I\times R(V_\xi)$ for some $\xi$; its image by $h$ lies in $R(V_{\xi+1})\subseteq R(V)$. An infinite cardinal's initial ordinal has no last element, so $\xi+1<\lambda$ whenever $\xi<\lambda$. We have proved $h(I\times R(V))\subseteq R(V)$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.38, closing-up construction. SOURCE ERROR repaired: the printed alpha-stage construction gives at best size alpha; use the smaller preservation rank lambda < alpha instead.

proof.text: Let $S=V\cap X$. At the endpoint $1$, Step 7 gives $kr(R(V))=h_1(R(V))\subseteq R(V)$. Since $kr$ also lands in $R(X)\subseteq R(Y)$, property (2) of [lem-coef-presheaf-bounded-intersection-replacement] gives $kr(R(V))\subseteq R(V)\cap R(X)=R(S)$. The map $k:R(X)\hookrightarrow R(Y)$ is monic, so from $k(r(z))\in k(R(S))$ we cancel $k$ and obtain $r(z)\in R(S)$ for every $z\in R(V)$; thus $r$ restricts to $r_V:R(V)\to R(S)$, with $r_VR(S\hookrightarrow V)=1$. The homotopy $h$ restricts to $I\times R(V)\to R(V)$, with endpoints $1$ and $R(S\hookrightarrow V)r_V$; its restriction to $R(S)$ is constant by Step 5. Consequently $R(S)\hookrightarrow R(V)$ is an $I$-homotopy equivalence. For each naive fibrant testing object $Z$, precomposition by $r_V$ is an inverse on $[-,Z]_I$ to precomposition by this inclusion: one composite is the identity strictly, and the other is the identity modulo the displayed homotopy after postcomposing with any map to $Z$. Hence $R(S)\hookrightarrow R(V)$ belongs to $W_I$.

source.place: Last paragraph of Lemma 2.4.38: use preservation of intersections to restrict r, and check the testing bijections directly.

proof.text: Naturality supplies the square with horizontal maps $\eta_S:S\to R(S)$ and $\eta_V:V\to R(V)$ and vertical inclusions $S\hookrightarrow V$ and $R(S)\hookrightarrow R(V)$. Both horizontal maps lie in $W_I$ by Steps 2-3, and the right map lies in $W_I$ by Step 8. Apply two-out-of-three to the equality of the two composites to conclude $S\hookrightarrow V\in W_I$. Step 7 gives $U\subseteq V$ and $|V|<\alpha$, and Step 3 chose $\alpha>|\operatorname{Mor}(A)|$ independently of $X,Y,U$. All subobject sets, ordinals, choices, images and unions used here are small in the input universe by the replacement statement and the fixed-universe well-ordering and recursion leaves. No model structure has been used.

source.place: Conclusion of Lemma 2.4.38, with the weak-equivalence square and all bounds checked.
